questions.question: _____ is the organization of data in a computer's memory or in a disk file.
questions.explanation: This is the standard textbook definition of a data structure (verified against course midterm).

questions.question: Which of the following best describes a non-primitive data structure?
options: Can store a set of homogeneous and heterogeneous elements
A relationship exists between its elements
Both 'can store homogeneous/heterogeneous elements' and 'a relationship exists between elements'
questions.correctAnswer: Both 'can store homogeneous/heterogeneous elements' and 'a relationship exists between elements'
questions.explanation: Non-primitive structures are NOT built-in types (so option 2 alone is false); they can hold homogeneous/heterogeneous data AND have relationships between elements, so the combined answer is correct.

questions.question: _____ is the ability to use an implemented data structure again and again in different places.
questions.explanation: Reusability is exactly this property — write a structure once, use it across many programs.
